step1.title: Welcome to Phentrieve
step1.content: This is your starting point for mapping research phenotype text to HPO terms. Let's take a quick tour of the main features!

step2.title: Enter research text
step2.content: Type or paste your research description here. You can describe phenotypes or research observations you want to map to HPO terms.

step3.title: Search for HPO terms
step3.content: Click this button to start the AI-powered analysis. Phentrieve will process your text and suggest relevant HPO terms.

step4.title: Review results
step4.content: Your search results will appear here, ranked by similarity. Each result shows the HPO term, its ID, and a similarity score.

step5.title: Advanced options
step5.content: Expand this section to access advanced search parameters like model selection and result limits.

step6.title: Collect terms
step6.content: Add relevant HPO terms to your collection with the add button next to each result. You can review and export them later.

step7.title: Your collection
step7.content: View, manage, and export your collected HPO terms here. You can export them as text or as a Phenopacket (JSON).

step8.title: Help and resources
step8.content: Access documentation, FAQs, and additional resources using the footer links. You can also view logs for debugging purposes.

whatIsPhentrieve.question: What is Phentrieve?
whatIsPhentrieve.answer:
Phentrieve is an AI-powered research tool that maps phenotype descriptions to standardized Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms. It supports phenotype annotation for research, education, benchmarking, and knowledge discovery.

Key features include:

  • Mapping research text to HPO terms
  • Semantic retrieval with biomedical embedding models
  • Support for multiple languages
  • User-friendly interface

howItWorks.question: How does Phentrieve work?
howItWorks.answer:
Phentrieve uses a pipeline of AI models and algorithms to process research phenotype text:

  1. Text Analysis: The system analyzes the input text using specialized biomedical language models
  2. Term Matching: It identifies potential HPO terms using semantic search and context-aware matching
  3. Ranking: The matches are ranked by relevance
  4. Results: The most relevant HPO terms are presented to the user

Results are suggestions and should be reviewed before any downstream use.

whoCanUse.question: Who can use Phentrieve?
whoCanUse.answer:
Phentrieve is for research and informational purposes only. It is NOT a clinical diagnostic tool.

Designed for:

  • Researchers: Standardizing phenotype descriptions in research studies
  • Bioinformaticians: Automated phenotype analysis in research datasets
  • Educators and students: Learning about HPO-based phenotype annotation
  • Curators: Literature review and research documentation

Important: Results must not be used for diagnosis, treatment, triage, or other clinical decision-making.

performance.question: What performance can I expect?
performance.answer:
Results on our benchmark set (hit rate at ranks 1, 3, and 5):

  • BioLORD-2023-M: HR{'@'}1=0.3333, HR{'@'}3=0.6667, HR{'@'}5=0.7778

Performance may vary based on the complexity and specificity of the input text.

similarityScore.question: What do the similarity scores mean?
similarityScore.answer:
Phentrieve uses cosine similarity to measure how closely your research phenotype text matches HPO terms. Scores range from 0.0 (no similarity) to 1.0 (maximum similarity).

Score ranges

  • 0.90 - 1.00: Excellent match - highly relevant
  • 0.75 - 0.89: High match - very relevant
  • 0.60 - 0.74: Moderate match - potentially relevant
  • 0.40 - 0.59: Low match - loosely related
  • 0.00 - 0.39: Poor match - not recommended

Technical details

Scores are calculated using cosine similarity between embedding vectors. A score of 1.0 means the embeddings point in the same direction, while 0.0 indicates no similarity.

Note: These scores represent semantic similarity in vector space, not clinical certainty.
